newsitem.title: UK: Survey shows UK manufacturing 25 pct foreign-owned.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows UK manufacturing 25 pct foreign-owned.

text.p: Foreign-owned multinational companies now account for a quarter of Britain's manufacturing base and one in three market leaders in UK manufacturing are not British-owned, a new survey shows.

The survey, conducted by Professor Steve Davies at the University of East Anglia and funded by the Economic and Social Research Council, found the number of foreign-owned firms in the UK's largest 100 producers rose from 18 in 1986 to 35 by 1993.
Over half those companies are North American but the European Union is providing increasing numbers of large multinationals in Britain -- 15 in the UK's top 100.

"The number of large multinational EU-owned firms with leading market shares increased from 13 to 27 in the period, a remarkable testament to the effects of 1992 and the introduction of the Single European Market," Davies said.

Davies said high multinational penetration may not be good for competition. "Our findings show that there are global oligopolies in which significant proportions of trade flows are between the firms themselves."
He also noted that of the British-owned firms in the top 100, 10 are recently privatised.
